about: Numbers the law-reach group B handlers use (src/core2/law-reach/group-b*.ts): who a policy reaches, the terms it sets and how a budget line's money reaches what it pays for. Each is tagged SOURCED (with citation), ESTIMATED (with source and spread) or TUNABLE (with the spread it's checked against).

daysPerYear.source: Calendar year (the core's calendar-day wage average, src/core2/modules/residents.ts).

centsPerDollar.source: U.S. currency; the core keeps money in cents (minor units).

reviewEveryMonths.source: How often a policy in force re-checks who it reaches (ages, income and work hours change). Monthly matches the monthly eligibility reporting most benefit programs use (7 CFR 273.12; 42 CFR 435.916 allows changes reported any time).

povertyGuidelineFirstPersonDollars.source: HHS 2025 poverty guidelines, 48 contiguous states and D.C., one person (90 FR 5917, Jan. 17, 2025). Alaska and Hawaii use their own rows (povertyGuidelineByState).

povertyGuidelinePerAddedPersonDollars.source: HHS 2025 poverty guidelines, each additional person, 48 contiguous states and D.C. (90 FR 5917).

medicaidExpansionIncomeShare.source: 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(10)(A)(i)(VIII) and 1396a(e)(14)(I): 133% of the poverty line plus the 5-point income disregard.

medicaidMonthlyMedicalDollars.source: BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey 2024, Table 1800 (national): prescription drugs $658 plus medical supplies $233 a year per consumer unit, over 12 months. It stands for the medical spending a covered adult no longer pays.

medicaidWorkHoursPerMonth.source: Pub. L. 119-21 (2025), sec. 71119 (42 U.S.C. 1396a(xx)): 80 hours a month of work, community service or school.

medicaidWorkExemptChildBelow.source: Pub. L. 119-21 (2025), sec. 71119: parents and caretakers of a dependent child 13 or younger are exempt.

snapWorkHoursPerWeek.source: 7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(2): 20 hours a week of work or a work program.

snapWorkTimeLimitMonths.source: 7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(2): an able-bodied adult without dependents who is not working 20 hours a week gets benefits for 3 months in any 36-month period.

snapWorkTimeLimitWindowMonths.source: 7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(2): the 36-month period the 3-month limit counts within.

snapWorkAgeFrom.source: 7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(3) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 (2025), sec. 10102: ages 18 through 64.

snapWorkAgeBelow.source: 7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(3) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 (2025), sec. 10102: ages 18 through 64.

snapWorkExemptChildBelow.source: 7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(3) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 (2025), sec. 10102: a household member under 14 exempts the adult.

assistanceIncomeShare.source: 7 U.S.C. 2014(c): SNAP gross income limit, 130% of the poverty line (the common test for means-tested assistance).

preschoolStateSpendingPerChildDollars.source: NIEER, The State of Preschool 2024 (2023-24 school year): state spending per enrolled child, $7,888 (all sources, $8,857).

preschoolEnrolledShare.source: Boston's universal preschool enrolled about 70% of four-year-olds (Gray-Lobe, Pathak and Walters 2023); the national rate without a universal program is 37% of four-year-olds and 8% of three-year-olds (NIEER 2024). Spread 0.4 to 0.9.

preschoolAgeFrom.source: NIEER, The State of Preschool 2024: state pre-K programs serve 3- and 4-year-olds.

preschoolAgeBelow.source: NIEER, The State of Preschool 2024: state pre-K programs serve 3- and 4-year-olds.

schoolAgeFrom.source: NCES, State Education Practices table 5.1: compulsory and kindergarten entry ages, 5 through 17.

schoolAgeBelow.source: NCES, State Education Practices table 5.1: compulsory and kindergarten entry ages, 5 through 17.

collegeAgeFrom.source: NCES, Digest of Education Statistics 2023, table 303.50: most undergraduates are 18 to 24.

collegeAgeBelow.source: NCES, Digest of Education Statistics 2023, table 303.50: most undergraduates are 18 to 24.

adultAge.source: Age of majority in the states (the age a household's adults are counted from).

drivingAge.source: FHWA Highway Statistics 2023, table DL-20: licensed drivers by age start at 16.

transitRiderAgeFrom.source: Most U.S. transit agencies carry children under 5 free with a paying rider (APTA fare survey 2023); a fare-free policy reaches riders 5 and older.

teacherMinimumSalaryDollars.source: Arkansas LEARNS Act (Act 237 of 2023): minimum teacher salary $50,000; New Mexico HB 13 (2022): level-one license floor $50,000.

schoolCompensationShare.source: NCES, Digest of Education Statistics 2023, table 236.10: salaries and benefits are about 80% of public school current expenditures.

healthCompensationShare.source: Census Bureau, 2022 Annual Survey of Public Employment and Payroll (health and hospital payroll) against the 2022 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances (health and hospital spending).

voucherAmountDollars.source: EdChoice, The ABCs of School Choice 2025: average education savings account and voucher amounts run about $4,000 to $10,000 a student.

transitFareboxPerResidentDollars.source: FTA National Transit Database 2023: fare revenue about $9.5 billion over 335 million residents; the public money that replaces fares when they end.

mileageFeeCentsPerMile.source: Oregon OReGO and Utah Road Usage Charge per-mile rates, 2024-25 (about 1 to 2.5 cents a mile).

broadbandMonthlyDollars.source: Entry tiers of municipal broadband utilities, 2024 (Institute for Local Self-Reliance community network list): about $40 to $90 a month.

highwayShareShifted.source: Share of the highway line an act moves to transit. Checked against flexible-funding transfers (FHWA flex funding reports 2019-2023: states moved a few percent up to about a quarter of eligible highway funds to transit).

stateFlatIncomeTaxPercent.source: Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets 2025: flat-rate states range from 2.5% to 4.95%.

localFlatIncomeTaxPercent.source: Tax Foundation, Local Income Taxes (2019 update): city and county income taxes run about 0.5% to 3.9%.

propertyTaxGrowthCapShare.source: California Constitution art. XIII A (Proposition 13): 2% a year on assessed value; Lincoln Institute, Significant Features of the Property Tax (2023): levy and assessment caps of 2% to 5%.

pensionShortfallPerResidentDollars.source: Pew Charitable Trusts, The State Pension Funding Gap (2023), and Equable Institute, State of Pensions 2024: state and local contributions fell about $20 to $45 billion short of the actuarially determined contribution, about $60 to $135 per resident.

reserveShareOfSpending.source: GFOA best practice, Fund Balance Guidelines for the General Fund (2015): unrestricted fund balance of no less than two months of regular operating spending.

groceryShareOfRetailSales.source: BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey 2024 (data/research/core-figures/P0-1/ce-region-categories-2024.json): households' retail purchases in the opening are food at home ($6,224 a year) and apparel and services ($2,001), so food at home is 6,224 / 8,225 of what retail sellers sell households. State exemptions cover unprepared food only; the share is the same everywhere.

cleanElectricityPriceShare.source: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, U.S. State Renewables Portfolio and Clean Electricity Standards: 2023 Status Update: compliance costs about 3% to 4% of average retail electricity bills.

carbonPricePerTonDollars.source: Washington Climate Commitment Act auction settlement prices 2023-2024 (about $25 to $63 a ton); California-Quebec cap-and-trade 2024 (about $30 to $42).

householdTonsPerYear.source: EIA, Energy-Related CO2 Emissions by sector 2023: residential plus personal-vehicle emissions per household, about 6 to 16 tons a year.

groundwaterWithdrawalShare.source: Kansas Local Enhanced Management Areas (K.S.A. 82a-1041) and Nebraska natural resources district allocations: limits cut pumping by about 5% to 40% from recent use.

bottleDepositCents.source: Container Recycling Institute, bottle bill states 2024: the common deposit is 5 cents (10 cents in Michigan and Oregon).

graduatedSchedules.about: The graduated schedule a graduated-income-tax act sets where the level had a flat tax or none (single filer; dollars and percents). ESTIMATED from the median of graduated states (Tax Foundation 2025) and of graduated city taxes; spread: top rates 4.5% to 7% (state) and 1.5% to 3% (local).
